items.premise: robots.txt line 99 `Disallow: /.well-known/` under `User-agent: *` blocks every compliant crawler from the exact directory agents.json (discovery.llmsTxt/llmsFull/entityGraph) and llms.txt advertise as the AI-discovery corpus — the CANON-048 GEO/AEO investment is self-nullified for well-behaved readers.
items.recipe: Insert a targeted Allow block for the four public files (llms.txt, llms-full.txt, entity-graph.json, security.txt) above the broad Disallow — crawlers honor most-specific match — keeping the rest of .well-known private. Add a build:check contract asserting every /.well-known/ URL referenced by agents.json + llms.txt is robots-Allowed, so the two surfaces can never contradict again (cross-surface coherence gate pattern).
items.outcome: info-finding: AI agents and search engines can actually fetch the citable corpus they are pointed to — restores the GEO/AEO citation surface.

items.recipe: Keep Play as the gold primary (games are the soul), promote Join The Vault to the accent-filled second slot, demote Map the Studio to secondary third. Track via existing data-track-event funnel counters (home_hero_member_click vs home_hero_atlas_click) in funnel-summary.

items.premise: Homepage field LCP p75 is 2,727ms (102 samples) — over the 2,500ms CWV budget on the highest-traffic route. The LCP image is a preloaded 5.2KB avif, so the delay is parse/render cost: the document is 138,211 bytes with a 54,149-byte inline <style> (39% of the doc) parsed before the hero paints. Lab perf 0.78 sits 0.02 above its 0.76 floor — zero headroom.
items.recipe: Split the inline <style>: keep above-the-fold shell + hero rules inline, move below-the-fold homepage section styles into the already-async external stylesheet path. Measure before/after with local Lighthouse; ship only if lab LCP improves and no FOUC on the fold. Shell-hash rotation cost is expected — pre-push perf trace per memory.
items.outcome: conversion: the front door reliably passes Core Web Vitals; mobile first-visit bounce pressure drops on the primary acquisition surface.

items.premise: build:check:steps (186 steps) runs check-cta-impression-contracts.mjs and check-session-state-contract.mjs twice each — byte-identical commands executed in full both times by run-build-check.mjs (no memoization). Pure wall-clock waste on a gate that runs many times per session.

items.recipe: Remove the later occurrence of each duplicate; add a self-check in run-build-check (or a build:check contract) that fails on duplicate identical steps so the chain can't silently re-accumulate them.

The coverage report ranks assets/ambient-loader.js (18.5KB, query-param/viewport/session gated) the #1 split candidate. INP on '/' and /universe/ is inputDelay-dominant (210ms / 694ms) — consistent with early main-thread contention from always-on shell script execution.

items.outcome: speed: ~18KB+ less shell JS parsed/executed on typical routes, cutting inputDelay-phase INP on the highest-traffic pages.

items.premise: supabase/config.toml pins verify_jwt for only 4 of 13 deployed functions (create-checkout, stripe-webhook, assign-discord-role, odds); the comment at line 69-70 states pinning exists precisely to stop a redeploy silently flipping the gateway posture — that protection is missing for the other 9 (ask-ignis, create-gift-checkout, customer-portal-session, semantic-search, eternal-intelligence, send-investor-digest, send-member-newsletter, send-push, upload-investor-doc).
liveEvidence: memory: feedback_supabase_verify_jwt_pin_config (S-prior 401 incident from unpinned flag)
items.recipe: Determine each function's intended posture from its in-code auth (getUser/authHeader/public+rate-limit) and declare all 13 explicitly in config.toml so git is the single source of truth.
items.outcome: trust: auth posture can no longer drift silently on redeploy; the JWT gate is auditable in git.

items.premise: The Layer-2 portal gate (worker line ~1024) returns Response.redirect(302) directly, bypassing withSecurityHeaders — no Cache-Control: no-store. CACHE_RULES mark bare paths cache-eligible, so a gate redirect can be stored and replay a 'go sign in' bounce after the member has authenticated (the exact cacheable-auth-gate trap from the S-prior 301 incident, in its 302 form).
items.recipe: Rebuild the gate response with explicit Cache-Control: no-store (+ Vary: Cookie) headers; extend tests/redirects.spec.js (or the worker unit spec) to assert no-store on the gate path.
items.outcome: conversion+trust: members never hit a stale sign-in bounce; no shared-cache gate leakage.

items.premise: nav-sheet.js buildBody() sources links via querySelectorAll('.nav-item') + '.nav-dropdown a' — the Home link is a bare anchor child of #nav-menu, so the 50% sheet cohort gets no Home entry while the classic drawer includes it (drawer CSS explicitly handles 'bare links like Home').
items.recipe: Prepend a Home entry in buildBody() cloned from navMenu.querySelector(':scope > a'); keep it cohort-consistent with the drawer ordering.
items.outcome: info-finding: sheet-cohort mobile visitors get a discoverable route home, matching the drawer cohort.

items.outcome: trust: conversion-critical redirect surface locked against silent breakage.

items.premise: login.html (committed, served) loads https://obeliskgate.com/auth-client.js, but obeliskgate.com appears in neither THIRD_PARTY_SCRIPT_SOURCES nor BASE_CONNECT_SOURCES in config/csp-policy.mjs — and the Worker strips any page-level CSP, so under the enforced Worker CSP the sign-in script and its callback are blocked. Scoped strictly as a CSP-coverage prereq for the already-committed page, NOT the gated Obelisk provider flip.

items.recipe: Add https://obeliskgate.com to script-src + connect-src in csp-policy.mjs (single source feeds worker CSP); note in DECISIONS that this un-blocks the page without flipping the provider decision.
items.outcome: trust: the committed sign-in entry point loads under CSP instead of failing closed.

items.premise: sitemap.xml:676 advertises /studio-hub/ which is simultaneously robots-Disallowed (robots.txt:96) and 301-redirected to the hub subdomain by the Worker — a self-contradictory crawl signal that Search Console flags as 'Submitted URL blocked by robots.txt'.
